episode_title: From Video Hosting to Video Platform with Wistia's Co-Founders

real_qa.q: What was Wistia's original vision when the company was founded?
real_qa.r: Wistia was originally conceived as a competition website for filmmakers, where big brands would post video production challenges and filmmakers could submit ads. This vision lasted about one month before the founders pivoted, realizing they had no connections to big brands. They then shifted focus to helping businesses use video, which remains their mission today.

real_qa.q: When did Wistia expand from video hosting to add editing, recording, and live capabilities?
real_qa.r: Wistia maintained a focused video hosting strategy from 2007 to 2021—an extremely long period. The expansion decision came after COVID-19, when the company observed that people started seeing their computers as cameras and expectations shifted rapidly for who should create video. This insight, combined with hundreds of customer interviews, convinced the founders that the moment had come to expand beyond pure hosting.
real_qa.requete: Wistia when expanded platform editing live

real_qa.q: How did Wistia's product launch velocity change after adopting a new company culture focused on rapid shipping?
real_qa.r: In 2022, Wistia delivered 12 product launches that were communicated to customers. After shifting the culture in October 2022 to prioritize shipping every two weeks rather than perfecting roadmaps, the company achieved 73 launches in 2023. By the time of this episode, they had already exceeded 100 launches for the current year—a dramatic acceleration driven by removing the requirement for roadmap approval and empowering teams to ship value quickly.

real_qa.q: What was the hardest challenge in transitioning Wistia from a point solution to a full platform from a marketing perspective?
real_qa.r: The hardest challenge is that it takes a very long time to shift market perception. Wistia had been known as a video hosting provider for more than a decade, so even after launching live and other features, the company had to repeatedly communicate these changes to the market. The founders noted they historically got bored easily with messaging and wanted to tell new stories, but actually needed to keep educating the market about the platform expansion due to massive lag in perception.
real_qa.requete: Wistia marketing transition point solution platform perception

real_qa.q: What is the biggest opportunity Wistia sees in B2B video marketing today?
real_qa.r: The biggest opportunity is building personal brands alongside B2B company brands. Social media algorithms have changed, making it almost impossible to get organic reach on branded accounts—companies now have to pay. However, individual accounts still get organic reach, and consumers trust and filter content through influencers and individuals rather than corporate brands, making personal brand building essential for B2B companies to explore.
real_qa.requete: B2B video marketing personal brands opportunity

real_qa.q: What video problem is Wistia most excited to solve for customers in the coming year?
real_qa.r: Wistia is working on atomization—making it easier for one person to extract multiple clips from a single video, find the right segments, edit them easily, and keep them on brand. The company is also leveraging its live product (in market for two years) to help customers with pre-event workflow, the live event itself, and post-event content atomization, creating an integrated platform experience.

guest.bio_context: Chris Savage is co-founder of Wistia, a video hosting and platform company he started with Brendan Schwartz. He has been leading the company's evolution from a point solution video hosting provider to a comprehensive video platform with editing, recording, and live capabilities since its founding.

real_quote: We basically said okay roadmaps you own it, we want you to ship every two weeks something of value to the customer.

COVID-19 triggered the decision to expand platform capabilities

2023: 73 product launches after cultural shift in October 2022
Current year: over 100 product launches already achieved
Wistia's live product has been in market for two years
Core customer base: B2B marketers at 50 to 200 person companies
